parameters.jsCode: const s=$input.first().json;if(!Array.isArray(s.leads)||s.leads.length<1||s.leads.length>5000)throw Error('Provide 1–5000 lead records');if(!['email','domain'].includes(s.deduplicateBy))throw Error('deduplicateBy must be email or domain');return s.leads.map((lead,i)=>({json:{lead,row:i+1,mode:s.deduplicateBy}}));

return $input.all().map(({json:r})=>{const l=r.lead&&typeof r.lead==='object'&&!Array.isArray(r.lead)?r.lead:{};const text=x=>typeof x==='string'?x.trim():'';const email=text(l.email).toLowerCase();let domain='',problem='';const website=text(l.website);if(website){try{const u=new URL(/^[a-z][a-z0-9+.-]*:/i.test(website)?website:'https://'+website);if(!['http:','https:'].includes(u.protocol)||u.username||u.password||!u.hostname.includes('.'))throw Error();domain=u.hostname.toLowerCase().replace(/^www\./,'');}catch{problem='Invalid website';}}return {json:{row:r.row,company:text(l.company),email,website,domain,validEmail:email.length<=254&&/^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/.test(email),problem,mode:r.mode}};});

const seen=new Map();return $input.all().map(({json:r})=>{let status='accepted',reason='',duplicateOf='';const key=r.mode==='email'?r.email:r.domain;if(!r.validEmail){status='review';reason='Missing or invalid email syntax';}else if(r.problem||(r.mode==='domain'&&!r.domain)){status='review';reason=r.problem||'Website domain required for domain deduplication';}else if(seen.has(key)){status='duplicate';reason='Repeated '+r.mode;duplicateOf=seen.get(key);}else{seen.set(key,r.row);}const safe=v=>typeof v==='string'&&/^[=+@\-\t\r]/.test(v)?"'"+v:v;return {json:Object.fromEntries(Object.entries({row:r.row,company:r.company,email:r.email,website:r.website,domain:r.domain,status,reason,duplicateOf}).map(([k,v])=>[k,safe(v)]))};});

# Clean and deduplicate a lead list with Edit Fields and export a review CSV

## Who is this for?
Researchers and small agencies cleaning a lead list before importing it into a CRM.

## What it does
Normalizes email addresses and website hostnames, checks basic email syntax, and marks repeated emails or website hosts. Every input row stays in the export with an accepted, duplicate or review status and an explanation. The first valid occurrence wins. A malformed record is sent for review instead of silently dropped. Download the result as a CSV and filter by status before importing it elsewhere.

## Setup
Run the sample once with Execute workflow. Open Edit lead list and rules, replace the fictional leads array with your own records, and select email or domain deduplication. Each record may contain company, email and website. Keep the field names unchanged. Run again and download the file from Export lead review CSV.

## Requirements and customization
Only built-in nodes are used; no accounts, API keys or paid services are required. Up to 5000 rows are supported per run. Replace the sample node with your own data source if needed. Matching happens inside the current run, not against a persistent CRM. Email checks are syntactic only: they do not verify mailbox delivery. Domain matching uses exact normalized hosts, not registrable-domain inference. The template never sends email.

## 1. Configure
Run once with the fictional sample. Edit the JSON settings in the Edit Fields node. No credentials required.

## 2. Validate and process
Invalid configuration stops with a clear error. Inspect each named processing step to understand the transformation.

## 3. Download
Open the final node → Output → Binary → Download. Review the CSV before using it in another system.
